component.name: langchain4j-agent
component.title: LangChain4j Agent
component.description: Send a message to an AI agent of LangChain4j, which can call Camel routes and MCP servers as tools, and return its answer.
component.label: ai

agent.description: The agent that answers the messages, an org.apache.camel.component.langchain4j.agent.api.Agent. It takes precedence over agentConfiguration, and agentFactory takes precedence over it.

agentConfiguration.description: The settings of LangChain4j (chat model, chat memory, tools, RAG, guardrails, and so on) from which the producer creates the agent: an AgentWithMemory when a ChatMemoryProvider is set, otherwise an AgentWithoutMemory. The agent and agentFactory options take precedence over it.

agentFactory.description: The factory whose createAgent method the producer calls for each message, to create the agent that answers it. It takes precedence over agent and agentConfiguration.

compensateOnToolErrors.label: producer
compensateOnToolErrors.description: Whether LangChain4j runs the compensating actions when a tool fails: the methods annotated with CompensateFor for the tools that already ran. When set, it replaces the value of the agentConfiguration. Only works when Camel creates the agent, from agentConfiguration or provider.

configuration.description: The configuration shared by the endpoints. Each endpoint starts from a copy of it.

executeToolsConcurrently.label: producer
executeToolsConcurrently.description: Whether LangChain4j runs the tools that the model requests in one response concurrently, on the executor of the agentConfiguration or else on a Camel thread pool; each route tool runs on a copy of the exchange. When set, it replaces the value of the agentConfiguration. Only works when Camel creates the agent, from agentConfiguration or provider.

jsonSchema.description: The JSON schema that the answer of the model must follow, inline or as a resource (classpath:, file:, ...). Camel sends it to the model as the response format, and the body is the answer as JSON text. Only works when Camel creates the agent, from agentConfiguration or provider, and not together with outputClass: otherwise the producer fails to start.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

maxToolCallingRoundTrips.label: producer
maxToolCallingRoundTrips.description: The maximum number of tool-calling round trips per message, each one model call and the tools that this call requests. A value above 0 replaces the value of the agentConfiguration; with 0, that value applies, or the LangChain4j default when it is not set either. Only works when Camel creates the agent, from agentConfiguration or provider.

outputClass.description: The Java class, a POJO with public fields or getters, from which Camel derives the JSON schema that the answer of the model must follow. The body is the answer as JSON text, not an instance of the class. Only works when Camel creates the agent, from agentConfiguration or provider, and not together with jsonSchema: otherwise the producer fails to start.

tags.description: A comma-separated list of tags. The routes that start from an ai-tool endpoint with one of these tags are offered to the model as tools. The CamelLangChain4jAgentExcludeTags header removes tags from this list for one message.

toolSearch.label: producer
toolSearch.description: Whether to leave the route tools with searchable=true and the MCP tools out of the first request to the model, and give the model one search tool (tool_search_tool) to find them; the other route tools and the customTools of the agentConfiguration are always sent. It controls what the model sees, not what it may call, and does not search a tool provider set outside Camel. Only works when Camel creates the agent, from agentConfiguration or provider.

toolSearchEmbeddingModel.label: producer
toolSearchEmbeddingModel.description: The LangChain4j embedding model that turns the tool descriptions and the search query into vectors. Required when toolSearchStrategy is VECTOR, and not used otherwise.

toolSearchMaxResults.label: producer
toolSearchMaxResults.description: The maximum number of tools that one call of the search tool returns, at least 1. Route tools and MCP tools are ranked together.

toolSearchStrategy.label: producer
toolSearchStrategy.description: How tool search ranks route and MCP tools. 'KEYWORD' matches the tool name and description. 'VECTOR' uses cosine similarity and requires toolSearchEmbeddingModel. Vector search does not fall back to keyword search.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

mcpClients.label: advanced
mcpClients.description: The MCP (Model Context Protocol) clients, of type dev.langchain4j.mcp.client.McpClient, whose tools are offered to the model, as references to beans in the registry, for example #myMcpClient1,#myMcpClient2. The producer does not close them.

mcpServer.label: advanced
mcpServer.description: The MCP servers whose tools are offered to the model, as mcpServer.myServer.myProperty=myValue, where myServer is the name of the server; the producer creates a client per server when it starts and closes it when it stops. The properties are transportType (stdio by default, or http or streamableHttp, which both use the Streamable HTTP transport), command (comma-separated, for stdio), environment.myKey=myValue (for stdio), url (for HTTP), timeout (in seconds, 60 by default), logRequests, logResponses, and oauthProfile (the camel-oauth profile that supplies a bearer token for HTTP). This is a multi-value option with prefix: mcpServer.

baseUrl.label: model
baseUrl.description: The URL of the provider's API (http://localhost:11434 for a local Ollama), when the model is created from the provider. The provider's default when not set.

modelName.label: model
modelName.description: The name of the model at the provider (qwen2.5, gpt-4o-mini, ...), when the model is created from the provider.

provider.label: model
provider.description: The LangChain4j provider of the chat model that drives the agent, to create the model from the options here (modelName, baseUrl, apiKey, temperature, timeout, and provider-specific model.* properties) instead of an AgentConfiguration bean. The LangChain4j module of the provider (dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-ollama, ...) must be on the classpath; the Camel CLI downloads it. Ignored when agent, agentFactory or agentConfiguration is set. For a provider not listed, set customProvider instead.

temperature.label: model
temperature.description: The sampling temperature of the model, when the model is created from the provider.

timeout.label: model
timeout.description: The request timeout of the model (30s, 2m), when the model is created from the provider.

customProvider.label: model,advanced
customProvider.description: The fully qualified class name of the LangChain4j model class of a provider that is not listed in provider (dev.langchain4j.model.jlama.JlamaChatModel), created from the options here through its builder() as a listed provider is. Set either provider or customProvider.

modelProperties.label: model,advanced
modelProperties.description: Provider-specific properties of the model, set on the model's builder as they are (model.numPredict=512 for Ollama, model.maxTokens=1024 for OpenAI), when the model is created from the provider. This is a multi-value option with prefix: model.

apiKey.label: model,security
apiKey.description: The API key or access token of the provider, when the model is created from the provider.

CamelLangChain4jAgentSystemMessage.description: The system message that the agent sends to the model with the user message. Not used when the body is an AiAgentBody, which holds its own system message.

CamelLangChain4jAgentMemoryId.description: The id of the conversation in the chat memory, required by an agent with a ChatMemoryProvider and not used by an agent without one. Not used when the body is an AiAgentBody, which holds its own memory id.

CamelLangChain4jAgentUserMessage.description: The text of the user message that goes with a file, bytes or a stream in the body. With a text body, this header replaces the text of the body. Not used when the body is an AiAgentBody.

CamelLangChain4jAgentMediaType.description: The media type (MIME type) of a file, bytes or a stream in the body, for example image/png. It takes precedence over the content type headers and over the file name extension.

CamelLangChain4jAgentExcludeTags.description: A comma-separated list of tags to remove from the tags option for this message. A route tool is still offered when another of its tags remains.

CamelLangChain4jAgentExcludeMcpServers.description: A comma-separated list of MCP server names whose tools the model is not offered for this message. The name is the key of the McpClient, or myServer of the mcpServer option.

CamelLangChain4jAgentFinishReason.description: The reason why the model stopped generating the answer: STOP, LENGTH, TOOL_EXECUTION, CONTENT_FILTER, or OTHER.

CamelLangChain4jAgentInputTokenCount.description: The number of input tokens, summed over all model calls for the message.

CamelLangChain4jAgentOutputTokenCount.description: The number of output tokens, summed over all model calls for the message.

CamelLangChain4jAgentTotalTokenCount.description: The number of input and output tokens, summed over all model calls for the message.

CamelLangChain4jAgentRequestModel.description: The name of the model that the request went to, read from the chat model of the agent, or unknown when Camel cannot read it.

CamelLangChain4jAgentResponseModel.description: The name of the model that answered. The producer does not set it, as the Result of LangChain4j does not hold it.

CamelLangChain4jAgentSources.description: The contents that the retrieval augmentor (RAG) of the agent retrieved for the message, if any.

CamelLangChain4jAgentToolExecutions.description: The tool executions, each with its request and result, that the agent ran for the message, if any.

CamelLangChain4jAgentModerationFlagged.description: Set to true when the moderation model of the agent flags the user message, and the exchange fails with a ModerationException. Not set otherwise.

producerIn.description: The user message as text, or an AiAgentBody with the user message, the system message, the memory id and a content. Bytes, a stream, a file of the file consumers, a java.io.File or a java.nio.file.Path is sent as an image, audio, video, PDF or text content (JSON, XML and YAML as text), after the text of the CamelLangChain4jAgentUserMessage header or alone without it; bytes and a stream need the CamelLangChain4jAgentMediaType or Content-Type header. A Map or another object fails, and no body fails

producerOut.description: The answer of the agent as text, also with outputClass or jsonSchema: unmarshal the JSON to read its fields. The token counts, the finish reason, the sources and the tool executions are in headers

agentId.description: The id of the agent. When none of agent, agentFactory, agentConfiguration and provider is set, the producer looks up the bean of type Agent with this name in the registry.
